partner_context.their_ambition: You are the UAE's everyday super-app — rides, food, and the Careem Pay wallet in one place, woven into daily life across the Emirates.
partner_context.their_pressure: Your home ride-hail market is mature and intensely competitive. Your next growth comes from new surfaces and premium experiences inside the app — not from more cars on Sheikh Zayed Road.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: The UAE is a coastline of islands, creeks and marinas with a leadership that has set a quantified marine-mobility mandate. Navier gives you a foiling water tier — booked in your app — across the one surface no ride-hail player has claimed.

hero.title: Careem × Navier — the everyday app, now on the water
hero.subtitle: Careem owns daily mobility in the UAE. The Gulf coastline is the surface it hasn't claimed yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We add a Careem-branded foiling water tier across the UAE's creeks, bays and islands — booked in-app, premium, and zero-emission. Navier brings the software-defined fleet and the network playbook proven in the Maldives; Careem brings the UAE demand, the app, and Careem Pay. Together we turn marina-to-marina trips and island runs into fast, smooth, on-demand water journeys.

why_now: Dubai's Marine Transport Master Plan 2030 targets a 51% jump in marine users (14.7M → 22.2M/yr) and a 400% increase in passenger lines. The UAE leadership is actively pulling mobility onto the water, and a ~100-vessel Navier network is already ramping in the Maldives (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026). The in-app water tier is open — for now.

network_thesis.headline: The everyday app already owns UAE demand — the coastline is the surface Careem hasn't claimed yet.
network_thesis.body: Careem runs rides, food, and Careem Pay across the Emirates. Navier adds a foiling water tier on the same app: marina-to-marina hops, island resort transfers, and Sharjah–Dubai adjacency corridors booked in-app. Phase 1 lights the Dubai beachhead; Phase 2 widens the northern coast; Phase 3 opens cross-emirate and Oman gateways — cumulative on the map, exact on the cards.

proof_points.claim: The leadership has a quantified marine mandate.
proof_points.evidence: Dubai Marine Transport Master Plan 2030: +51% users to 22.2M/yr; passenger lines to 35 (+400%).

proof_points.claim: The network model is real and at scale.

proof_points.evidence: Careem operates across all seven emirates — the demand, the riders and Careem Pay are in place in every coastal market the water tier would serve.
Navier's Turkey factory sits a short sail from the Gulf — vessels, parts and service on the same side of the world as the fleet.

objections.concern: Is the range enough across the UAE?
objections.response: Intra-Dubai and island runs are a few nautical miles; even Dubai↔Abu Dhabi (~47 nm) sits inside the Pioneer II all-electric envelope, with Quanta-LR for anything longer — no charging infrastructure required.
Foiling cuts energy per mile dramatically and the cabin is climate-controlled; routing and scheduling flex around peak summer just as road mobility does.
A clear first-of-class path, software-defined controls, and an operating record in the US and the Maldives.

phases.label: Phase 1 — Dubai beachhead
phases.rationale: Launch where Careem demand is densest — Dubai Harbour, Pearl Jumeirah, and the brutal Sharjah waterfront commute — before extending to other emirates.
phases.narrative: Four Pioneer II vessels on Dubai and Sharjah's highest-demand coastal corridors, booked in the Careem app — proving the in-app water tier in the marine authority's flagship city.

phases.label: Phase 2 — the inter-emirate link
phases.rationale: Extend the proven Dubai model down the coast to Abu Dhabi's island-rich waterfront and connect the two emirates by sea — the everyday-app water layer for the whole UAE.
phases.narrative: We connect the demand centres: a coastal Dubai↔Abu Dhabi link, the brutal Sharjah↔Dubai commute solved over the water, and Abu Dhabi's Yas–Saadiyat–Lulu island mesh — one app, one wallet, three emirates.

phases.label: Phase 3 — the full-UAE water layer
phases.rationale: Complete the national layer: the northern emirates by Pioneer II along the Gulf coast, and a self-contained Pioneer II cluster on the Indian-Ocean east coast — Dibba, Khor Fakkan and Kalba — so every emirate Careem serves by road is now on the water.
phases.narrative: The water layer goes UAE-wide: Ras Al Khaimah on the northern Gulf coast, and a tight Pioneer II cluster on the Fujairah east coast — Dibba, Khor Fakkan and Kalba on the Gulf of Oman — every emirate Careem serves by road, now on the water.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling fleet, the Maldives-proven network playbook, captain training and the first-of-class certification path.
the_ask.partner_brings: You bring UAE demand and dispatch through the Careem app, Careem Pay, and your local relationships.
the_ask.next_step: A Dubai pilot MOU on three coastal corridors.

close.title: The everyday app, on the UAE's water.
close.body: Dubai proves it; the full-UAE network scales it. Careem's everyday demand meets the one surface no ride-hail player has claimed — the Gulf coastline.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Three forces just converged: the technology crossed from prototype to platform (10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out), decarbonization mandates turned legacy diesel fleets into stranded liabilities, and the hybrid removed the 'no charging at the islands' excuse. Autonomy is arriving on the water before the road. The marine layer is being claimed cluster-by-cluster right now.

end_state.headline: The water layer of the Careem super-app — UAE-wide, all seven emirates.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every UAE coastal market Careem already serves by road — Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah — wherever the Gulf or the Indian Ocean coast separates demand from destination.

steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II throughout — the Dubai↔Abu Dhabi trunk, intra-metro hops, and a self-contained Fujairah east-coast cluster (Dibba–Khor Fakkan–Kalba)
steady_state.tam_framing: The UAE moves tens of millions of premium ground trips a year through Careem; the water versions of those trips — Marina to Abu Dhabi, Dubai to RAK, across to Fujairah — are an unmonetised premium surface.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a UAE-wide water layer inside the Careem app: book a foiling vessel the same way you book a car, from any emirate to any coast.

deck_only.differentiation_vs_status_quo: UAE water transport today is mostly scheduled abras, ferries and dinner cruises. A foiling tier is on-demand, fast, near-silent and zero-emission — a premium mode, not a sightseeing boat.

revenue_potential.headline: The floor and the prize — every rung traces to grounded, sourced demand.
revenue_potential.modal_lead: We start from grounded corridor demand. Each step adds one realistic expansion lever — network width, induced demand, journey wallet, platform take.
revenue_potential.anchor_note: $131M/yr premium sea-transfer spend on sourced corridors today — the anchor every rung builds from.

whose_money_legend.navier_transport_revenue: Fare the Navier boats collect. This is the corridor P&L (atom.py). SOM/SAM rungs are in this unit.
whose_money_legend.journey_gmv: Total spend on the whole island journey flowing through the super-app: transport + food + stays + experiences + ads + parcel/logistics. Gross, all merchants. TAM rung is in this unit.
whose_money_legend.platform_take: The partner's (Grab's) own commission revenue on journey_gmv. Derived line — this is the number that makes a super-app care, not the boat fare.
